details:
Letters to Earth is an interactive web story in which the hardware NASA left on the Moon and Mars writes letters home: Surveyor 3, the Apollo 11 descent stage, ALSEP, the Lunar Roving Vehicle, the laser retroreflectors and the Viking landers. Each letter is based on real NASA mission data and explains what the machine did, why it stayed behind, and what it still teaches us.

How it works: a single web page drawn in real time on HTML Canvas with a hand-made felt, stop-motion look (12 fps). Original music and sound effects are synthesized in code with the Web Audio API, and narration uses the Web Speech API. It runs on computers, tablets and phones with no installation.

Benefits and impact: it brings NASA history and science to children aged 7-12 who are often left out. It works in 4 languages (English, Spanish, Portuguese, French). It has three reading modes: Watch, Listen (narrated scene descriptions for blind and low-vision users) and See (written sound captions for deaf users), plus keyboard navigation, screen-reader support and a reduced-motion option. Printable mini-books (student book with coloring pages and quiz challenges, and a teacher guide with learning goals, activities and sources) let classrooms without internet keep learning offline.

Creativity: instead of a list of facts, abandoned equipment becomes characters with feelings and a voice, turning "space junk" into heritage worth remembering.

Factors considered: accessibility, language barriers, low-connectivity schools, age-appropriate reading level, scientific accuracy, and a cohesive, calm visual style.

Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Canvas 2D, Web Audio API, Web Speech API, Python (PDF book generation), GitHub, Netlify, and Claude (Anthropic) as a coding assistant.
